newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway Dec oil output slips marginally from Nov.
newsitem.headline: Norway Dec oil output slips marginally from Nov.

text.p: Norwegian oil output slipped 0.3 percent to 3.10 million barrels per day (bpd) in December from a month earlier as several fields experienced production problems and brief shutdowns, a Reuters survey of operators in Norwegian waters showed.
Norway pumped 3.11 million bpd in November.

The December figure omits production from the Sleipner condensate developments. Operator Statoil said total liquid output -- stabilised oil and liquefied petroleum gases -- at Sleipner East and West amounted to 145,665 bpd, but due to technical difficulties the company was unable to provide a figure for condensate alone.
There were major variations in production at the Statfjord and Brage oilfields due to maintenance and well capacity problems, operators said.
Den norske stats oljeselskap AS attributed a 14 percent slip in Statfjord's output to well maintenance and a two-day shutdown at the development.

"Statfjord is in decline, which means that when there is a partial shutdown there's no excess capacity available to make up the difference," a Statoil spokeswoman said. "The field is back to full production now."
Well capacity problems at Brage knocked output down to 78,559 bpd from normal levels of 120,000 bpd. Norsk Hydro said the field returned to usual output at the end of December.
Hydro said a dip in average production at the Oseberg complex to 488,217 bpd from 495,595 bpd was due to a one-day maintenance shutdown.
Phillips said a series of technical difficulties and minor shutdowns caused Ekofisk production to slip to around 315,000 bpd from nearer 330,000 bpd in November.
Slightly lower flow at Saga Petroleum's two fields, Snorre and Tordis, was put down to "normal variation".
Heidrun in the Norwegian Sea bounced back to pump 242,115 bpd of acidic crude, 23 percent up on November when the installation suffered several days downtime due to the flare tip falling off.
